messages:
maria: Hey folks — spotted two issues in the Python onboarding that are blocking new users. The sample app link in the quickstart goes 404 and the env var used in the snippet doesn't match the SDK (users get a Missing API key error).

maria: repro steps: follow quickstart, set REDWOOD_API_TOKEN=... then run sample. it fails on auth. the docs show REDWOOD_API_TOKEN, but our SDK reads REDWOOD_API_KEY.

devex-bot: thanks for the report @maria — filing internal ticket: DEVEX-412. Can you paste the exact error you see? :mag:

maria: here's the traceback (shortened):
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "sample_app.py", line 22, in <module>
    client = Client()  # relies on env
  File "site-packages/redwood/client.py", line 45, in __init__
    raise MissingCredentialsError("No API key found in environment")
redwood.errors.MissingCredentialsError: No API key found in environment
```

maria: also the quickstart's repo link returns 404: https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples/python-quickstart -> 404

ryan: repro'd locally. Confirmed: docs reference REDWOOD_API_TOKEN, codebase expects REDWOOD_API_KEY. Pretty small fix. The 404 is because the samples repo got renamed last month -> should point to https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples-python/quickstart (new repo).

zach: fyi I hit another minor annoyance: the async example uses `async with Client()` but our AsyncClient doesn't implement __aenter__/__aexit__ typed as returning AsyncClient in stubs, so linters/IDE complain. We should update typing so `async with Client()` has proper typing for the context manager.

maria: oof good call. user-facing fixes we should do:
- update quickstart page to use REDWOOD_API_KEY or make SDK accept REDWOOD_API_TOKEN too (backcompat)
- update the sample link to the new repo path
- fix type stubs for AsyncClient context manager

ryan: I'll open a docs PR for the env var + link. small patch. ETA today. I'll cc @docs-jen for typing guidance.

docs-jen: thanks @ryan! I can help with the type hints. For the env var, let's prefer REDWOOD_API_KEY as canonical; but we can add a small compat layer in client.init() to check REDWOOD_API_TOKEN and warn if present. That avoids breaking users who followed older docs.

zach: WDYT about raising a small deprecation warning if REDWOOD_API_TOKEN found, telling users to switch? That helps migrate without surprises.

docs-jen: yep, deprecation warning + docs note + changelog entry. I'll post a proposed typing change: in types.pyi add:
```
class AsyncClient:
    async def __aenter__(self) -> "AsyncClient": ...
    async def __aexit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb) -> None: ...
```

maria: thanks all. @ryan please drop the PR numbers here so support can triage incoming tickets. Also adding a short snippet we can paste to the docs to make it clearer:
```
# recommended env var
export REDWOOD_API_KEY="sk-..."
# compatibility: SDK will also look for REDWOOD_API_TOKEN and warn
```

ryan: PRs: docs fix -> #1894, compat shim + warning -> #1895, typing stub -> #1896. I'll add the new sample repo URL in the docs patch.

maria: great. once merged can someone ping #support so we can close the tickets from customers hitting this? :pray:

devex-bot: linked PRs #1894, #1895, #1896. When merged, will notify #support automatically.

zach: quick note for follow-up: add an e2e smoke test for quickstart sample that runs `python sample_app.py` in CI to detect link/usage drift; put it behind a small nightly job to avoid failing fast on transient network issues.

maria: that would help a lot. ok closing loop — thanks team :tada:
